ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

fullPassage:
Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more. He rushes to the other side of the net and challenges his dad to a match.

Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path.

Let's start with the path of avoidance. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. "Never mind," says his dad, "Try again. Practice makes perfect."

When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room.

His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough. "No, thanks," sighs the boy. "He's going to be better than me anyway." In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.

Let's rewind to the point when the boy first faces his dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, he picks up the ball and tries again anyway.

An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his dad. The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. His brother is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder.

The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He realizes how far he has come. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of improving his game. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph. He has become truly awesome!

You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!

Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged and helpless? The answer lies in resilience — the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties.

The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them.

Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.

questions.passage:
The boy who embraces the challenge picks up the ball and tries again anyway after being hit on the elbow.

(A) Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard.

(B) The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team.

(C) He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 실수 학습 → 지역팀(B) → 전국대회 결승(A) → 승리(C)
det.analysis:
✅ ② (B)-(A)-(C): 연습→지역팀→전국대회→결승 승리 순서
❌ ① (A)-(B)-(C): 전국대회가 연습보다 먼저 올 수 없음
❌ ③ (B)-(C)-(A): 승리(C)가 전국대회(A)보다 먼저 올 수 없음
❌ ④ (C)-(A)-(B): 역순, 시간 흐름 어긋남
det.tip: 시간 순서: 연습(B) → 전국대회 결승(A) → match point 승리(C)

❌ ② (A)-(C)-(B): 비유가 가장 먼저 올 수 없음
❌ ④ (C)-(B)-(A): 개발이 정의보다 먼저 올 수 없음
det.tip: 논리 순서: 문제 제기 → 개념 정의(B) → 구체 설명(C) → 비유(A)

❌ ① 앞: 아직 소년 소개 전
❌ ② 앞: 아직 집에 도착 안 함
❌ ③ 앞: 아직 탁구대 발견 전
det.tip: 삽입 문장의 excited는 탁구대 발견 직후 반응이므로 ③과 ④ 사이

questions.passage: ① The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. ② However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. ③ Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them. ④ Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.

❌ ① 앞: 회복 가능성 설명 전
❌ ② 앞: 아직 resilience 제약 설명 전
❌ ③ 앞: 아직 극복 설명 전

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ⓐ~ⓓ 모두 어법상 올바르다. 하지만 원문 대조 시 모두 정확하므로 '틀린 것 없음'이 아니라 가장 의심되는 것을 선택해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ 모두 올바름 — 함정 문제가 아닌 경우, 전부 문법적으로 정확
ⓐ gets hit: 수동 (get + p.p.)
ⓑ picks up: 구동사
ⓒ winning: keep + V-ing
ⓓ surprises: 3인칭 단수 현재
det.tip: get + p.p. = 수동, keep + V-ing = 계속, 3인칭 단수 -s 확인

questions.passage: The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is (A) [perfect / perfectly] normal to feel down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and (B) [overcome / overcoming] them. Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be (C) [exposed / exposing] to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 형용사 수식 부사 perfectly, (B) help + 원형/to-V에서 face and 병렬 overcome, (C) be exposed to 수동태
det.analysis:
✅ ④ perfectly — overcome — exposed: 원문 일치
❌ ① perfect — overcome — exposing: (A) 틀림
❌ ② perfectly — overcoming — exposed: (B) 틀림
❌ ③ perfect — overcoming — exposing: (A)(B)(C) 모두 틀림
det.tip: (A) 부사+형용사: perfectly normal, (B) 병렬: face and overcome, (C) 수동: be exposed to

questions.passage: The boy <u>ⓐ learns</u> from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is <u>ⓑ able</u> to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent <u>ⓒ to be</u> skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its <u>ⓓ breathing</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: hold one's breath(숨을 죽이다)에서 breath(명사)가 와야 한다. ⓓ breathing(동명사/현재분사)은 틀림.
det.analysis:
❌ ⓓ breathing: 원문은 breath(명사) → 고정 숙어 hold one's breath
✅ ⓐ learns: 3인칭 단수 현재 → 올바름
✅ ⓑ able: be able to → 올바름
✅ ⓒ to be: find + O + to be C → 올바름
det.tip: hold one's breath (숨을 참다) — breath(명사) ≠ breathing(동명사)

questions.passage: Think of it like building your body's immune system. In simple terms, resilience is not about being (B) [emotionless / emotional]: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 세균에 노출 exposed, (B) 감정 없는 것이 아님 emotionless, (C) 운동하는 것처럼 working out

✅ ① exposed — emotionless — working out: 원문 일치
❌ ② isolated: exposed의 반의어
❌ ③ emotional: emotionless와 반대 (not about being emotionless 구문)
❌ ④ giving up: 포기 → 문맥과 반대
det.tip: exposed to ↔ isolated from, emotionless ↔ emotional, working out ↔ giving up

✅ ② stronger: 더 강해지다 → 적절
✅ ③ adapt: 적응하다 → 적절

❌ ① 도전적 경험에 적응하는 능력이다: 원문 일치
❌ ② 인간은 압박과 어려움에서 회복할 수 있다: 원문 일치
❌ ④ 감정이 없는 것이 아니다: 원문 일치
det.tip: 이중 부정 주의: does not mean ~ never = 여전히 느낄 수 있다

ch: 인간은 압박과 어려움으로부터 회복할 수 있다.
회복탄력성이 있으면 스트레스나 불안을 전혀 느끼지 않는다.

questions.passage: ① Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges. ② The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop the skill of resilience. ③ However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious. ④ Professional athletes often earn millions of dollars through sponsorship and endorsement deals.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

det.korean: 본문 전체 주제: 회복탄력성(resilience) 개발. ④는 프로 선수의 수입에 관한 내용으로 주제와 무관.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ Professional athletes ~ endorsement deals: 회복탄력성과 무관한 내용
✅ ① 십대 도전 → 주제 도입
✅ ② 회복 가능성 → 주제 전개
✅ ③ 스트레스 느낄 수 있음 → 주제 심화
det.tip: 무관 문장 찾기: 주제(resilience)와 관련 없는 문장 선별

questions.passage: In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like __________ to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 근육을 키우기 위해 운동하는 것(working out)처럼 시간과 노력이 필요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② working out: 원문 일치, 운동-근육 비유
❌ ① taking a long rest: 쉬는 것 → 노력과 반대
❌ ③ following strict instructions: 지시 따르기 → 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ avoiding all pain: 고통 회피 → resilience 개념과 반대
det.tip: working out → muscles = experiencing difficulties → resilience (병렬 비유)

questions.passage: When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. He sets the paddle on the table, __________ (say), 'I have had enough,' and leaves for his room.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: 분사구문 — 패들을 내려놓으며 동시에 '충분히 했다'고 말하면서(saying)
det.analysis:
say → saying: 동시동작 분사구문
주절 주어(He)와 동일 → 접속사·주어 생략 + 동사 → 현재분사(-ing)
det.tip: 분사구문: 접속사 + 주어 생략 → V-ing (주절과 동시 동작 표현)

questions.passage: Think of it like __________ (build) your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: 전치사 like 다음 동명사 — 면역 체계를 구축하는 것처럼(building)
det.analysis:
build → building: 전치사(like) 다음에는 동명사(-ing)
Think of A like B → like + 동명사
det.tip: 전치사 + 동명사: like/for/of/without + V-ing

questions.passage: Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them. Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be __________ (expose) to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 쓰시오.

det.korean: be exposed to: 수동태. 세균에 '노출되다'이므로 과거분사 필요.
det.analysis:
expose → exposed: need to be + p.p. (수동태)
you(사람)가 세균에 노출되는 것이므로 수동
det.tip: be exposed to = ~에 노출되다 (수동태 + 전치사 to)
